sections.heading: Add specialist capacity. Keep the right delivery accountability.
sections.body:
Bring specialists across our five portfolios into your existing teams, or engage a managed delivery pod with agreed outcomes and governance. Choose the model according to the capability gap and the delivery responsibility you want to retain.

Choose [Staff augmentation](#staff-augmentation) or [Managed teams](#managed-teams). For centre ownership, explore [GCC BOT](/services/talent-advisory-gcc/gcc-build-operate-transfer).

sections.heading: Specialist capability across five portfolios
sections.description: Bring the right expertise to your next initiative. Confirm role mix, location, seniority and availability during scoping; this is not a live skills list.

sections.heading: Staff augmentation

items.title: You direct delivery
items.description: Specialists embedded in your teams, with delivery direction retained by you.
items.bullets:
Best fit – a specific capability or capacity gap in a client-led team
Your responsibility – backlog priorities, daily direction and acceptance of work
Linkfields scope – specialist sourcing and onboarding support as agreed

items.title: Agree the working boundaries
items.description: Define the role, skills evidence and working arrangements before mobilisation.
items.bullets:
Governance – named contacts, review cadence and escalation route
Acceptance – your delivery standards and review process
Change – agree role, capacity or replacement requests through the engagement process

sections.note: A start depends on availability, skills validation, contract scope, access and onboarding. Agree location and time-zone coverage. Staff augmentation does not establish an offshore centre.

items.title: Linkfields runs the delivery pod
items.description: Outcome-based delivery pods we run end to end, within the scope and responsibilities agreed for the engagement.
items.bullets:
Best fit – a defined delivery need you want a team to own
Linkfields responsibility – team coordination and delivery of agreed scope
Your responsibility – business priorities, timely decisions, inputs and acceptance

items.title: Make accountability explicit
items.description: Agree delivery measures, quality gates and change handling before work enters the pod.
items.bullets:
Governance – progress, risks, dependencies and escalation reviews
Acceptance – agreed deliverables and evidence at review gates
Change – assess scope, effort and acceptance impacts before approval

sections.heading: From a capability gap to a productive team

items.title: Define the capability brief
items.description: Describe the work, constraints and responsibilities the team needs to cover.

items.title: Agree the model
items.description: Choose client-directed specialists or a Linkfields-managed delivery pod.
items.bullets: Output – accountability, acceptance and commercial agreement

items.title: Select and onboard
items.description: Agree skills validation, access, induction and ways of working before delivery.

items.title: Deliver and review
items.description: Review progress, quality, capacity and change requests against agreed priorities.

sections.note: Illustrative, not client cases: an embedded specialist joins client-led quality engineering; a managed integration pod delivers agreed scope with client acceptance.

sections.heading: Build quality and security into the working model
sections.description: Agree how delivery IP supports quality and security within your approved environments, who operates it and which products require separate licensing.

items.title: testoriumz
items.description: Consider low-code testing, AI root-cause analysis and CI/CD integration where the team owns application assurance.

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: Consider composable applications where a delivery pod is building beyond the fit of ERP or CRM.

items.title: Governed, cyber-safe delivery
items.description: Agree access boundaries, code and release reviews, quality evidence and escalation responsibilities.
items.bullets:
Applicable IP – Automated Testing & Release Assurance Packs and Cyber-Safe Delivery
Scope question – who configures, operates and accepts each control?

items.title: Who directs the work and accepts it?
items.description: You direct embedded specialists and accept their work through your delivery process. For managed teams, Linkfields runs the agreed delivery scope while you provide business direction, decisions and acceptance. Record the split before work begins.

items.title: How are skills and onboarding agreed?
items.description: Agree the capability brief, skills evidence and validation approach; check availability during scoping. Before mobilisation, confirm access, induction, delivery standards and working arrangements. Record approval and escalation responsibilities, including replacement or transition arrangements.

items.title: How are access, locations and time zones handled?
items.description: Access follows the agreed data and security boundaries. Linkfields is headquartered in South Africa and has an offshore delivery centre in India; the assignment location, working hours and time-zone coverage are agreed for your engagement.

items.title: How does the delivery model affect fees?
items.description: Outcome-led delivery does not automatically mean outcome-based fees; commercials are agreed separately. A managed team is not automatically an infrastructure managed service. Fixed Price, Time & Materials, Managed Service, Dedicated Team and Outcome-Based are the commercial choices. Outcome-Based requires measurable outcomes and evidence.

items.title: What should we include in the enquiry?
items.description: Include your model (or Not sure), capability, desired start and delivery context. We can agree an NDA before detailed discovery. For centre ownership, see [GCC strategy](/services/talent-advisory-gcc/gcc-strategy-setup) or [BOT](/services/talent-advisory-gcc/gcc-build-operate-transfer).
